title: The Mystery Revealed
overview: Ephesians Chapter 3 unveils the profound mystery of the gospel that Paul, as a prisoner for Christ, was entrusted to proclaim: that Gentiles are fellow heirs with Jews in the promises of Christ. This chapter highlights the revelation of God's grace, the unity of all believers in one body, and the manifold wisdom of God displayed through the church. Paul’s heartfelt prayer for spiritual strength and comprehension of Christ’s love encourages believers to live rooted in faith and love. This chapter serves as a pivotal theological foundation for understanding the inclusive nature of salvation and the empowering presence of the Spirit in the believer’s life.
structure:
**Verses 1-6: The Revelation of the Mystery.** Paul introduces his role as a prisoner for the Gentiles and explains the divine revelation of the mystery that Gentiles are co-heirs with Jews, united in Christ by the gospel.

**Verses 7-13: Paul’s Ministry and Its Purpose.** Paul describes his calling and grace to preach the unsearchable riches of Christ, emphasizing the hidden wisdom of God now made known through the church, and encourages believers not to be discouraged by his sufferings.

**Verses 14-21: Paul’s Prayer for Spiritual Strength.** Paul prays for the believers to be strengthened by the Spirit, to have Christ dwell in their hearts through faith, and to grasp the vastness of Christ’s love, culminating in praise to God’s eternal glory through the church.

keyVerses.text: That the Gentiles should be fellowheirs, and of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the gospel:
keyVerses.significance: This verse reveals the groundbreaking truth that Gentiles are fully included in God's redemptive plan, sharing equally in the promises of Christ, which was a mystery previously hidden. It underscores the unity and equality of all believers in the body of Christ.

keyVerses.text: That he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man;
keyVerses.significance: Paul’s prayer for inner spiritual strength highlights the essential role of the Holy Spirit in empowering believers from within, enabling them to live out their faith effectively and withstand trials.

keyVerses.text: Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us,
keyVerses.significance: This verse affirms God’s unlimited power at work within believers, encouraging faith in His ability to accomplish far beyond human expectations through His Spirit.

keyVerses.text: In whom we have boldness and access with confidence by the faith of him.
keyVerses.significance: This verse emphasizes the confidence and boldness believers have to approach God through faith in Christ, highlighting the new relationship with God made possible by the gospel.

characters.name: Paul
characters.description: The apostle and author of Ephesians, Paul is portrayed as a prisoner for Christ who has been given the grace to reveal the mystery of the gospel to the Gentiles. His ministry, sufferings, and prayers demonstrate his deep commitment to the unity and spiritual growth of the church.

characters.name: God the Father
characters.description: Referred to as the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, He is the source of all spiritual blessings, the one who reveals the mystery of salvation, and the recipient of Paul’s prayers and praise.

characters.name: Jesus Christ
characters.description: Central to the mystery revealed, Christ is the foundation of the church, the one through whom all creation was made, and the source of the unsearchable riches and love that believers are called to comprehend and experience.

characters.name: The Holy Spirit
characters.description: The Spirit reveals the mystery to the apostles and prophets, strengthens believers inwardly, and empowers the church to display God’s manifold wisdom.

themes.description: This chapter focuses on the previously hidden truth that Gentiles are now included as co-heirs with Jews in Christ, emphasizing God’s sovereign plan to unite all believers into one body.
Paul’s prayer for believers to be strengthened by the Spirit highlights the necessity of divine empowerment for living a faithful Christian life rooted in love and faith.
The church’s role is to reveal the multifaceted wisdom of God to spiritual powers, demonstrating God’s eternal purpose and the glory of His grace through the unity of believers.
Through faith in Christ, believers have confident access to God’s presence, a theme that encourages perseverance and assurance in the Christian walk.

historicalContext: Ephesians was written by the Apostle Paul during his imprisonment, traditionally dated around AD 60-62, likely in Rome. The city of Ephesus was a major urban center in Asia Minor (modern-day Turkey), known for its temple to Artemis and diverse population including Jews and Gentiles. The early church faced challenges of unity and understanding the inclusion of Gentiles into God’s covenant promises. Paul’s letter addresses these issues by revealing the mystery of the gospel and encouraging spiritual maturity. Politically, the Roman Empire maintained control, and Christians were a minority group often misunderstood or persecuted, making Paul’s emphasis on boldness and access to God particularly poignant.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology emphasizes the sovereignty of God in revealing the mystery of salvation and the unity of Jews and Gentiles in Christ. It highlights the role of grace in Paul’s ministry and the believer’s spiritual strengthening by the Spirit as evidence of God’s covenant faithfulness.

Dispensationalists see this chapter as a key revelation of the current dispensation of grace, where Gentiles are grafted into the promises of God alongside Israel. They stress the distinct roles of Israel and the church but affirm the spiritual blessings available to all believers.

Early church fathers like Augustine interpreted this chapter as a profound exposition of the church’s unity and the spiritual riches found in Christ, encouraging believers to seek deeper knowledge of God’s love and to persevere in faith despite trials.

crossReferences.connection: Paul discusses Gentiles being grafted into the olive tree, paralleling Ephesians 3’s teaching on Gentiles as fellowheirs in Christ.
Reveals the mystery of Christ in believers, echoing the hidden wisdom now made known in Ephesians 3.
Paul’s experience of grace and strength in weakness complements the prayer for spiritual strength in Ephesians 3.
Encourages believers to approach God with confidence and boldness, similar to the access described in Ephesians 3:12.
Jesus promises the Holy Spirit to dwell within believers, paralleling the strengthening by the Spirit in Ephesians 3.

application: Recognize and embrace the unity of all believers in Christ, regardless of background.
Pray regularly for inner spiritual strength empowered by the Holy Spirit.
Approach God with confidence and boldness through faith in Jesus Christ.
Seek to comprehend and experience the vast love of Christ in daily life.
Persevere through trials, knowing they serve God’s greater purpose and glory.
Proclaim the unsearchable riches of Christ to others, especially those outside the faith.
conclusion: Ephesians Chapter 3 stands as a profound revelation of God’s inclusive plan of salvation, uniting Jews and Gentiles into one body through Christ. Paul’s heartfelt ministry, his sufferings, and his powerful prayer for spiritual strength remind believers of the immeasurable love and power available through faith. This chapter encourages Christians to live boldly and rooted in love, empowered by the Spirit, while giving glory to God’s eternal wisdom displayed in the church. It remains a vital foundation for understanding the gospel’s reach and the believer’s spiritual journey.
timeline: c. AD 60-62 - Paul’s Imprisonment in Rome and Writing of Ephesians

definitions.definition: A period or arrangement in God’s plan during which He administers His will in a particular way, especially relating to the unfolding of salvation history.
A divine truth previously hidden but now revealed by God, especially concerning the inclusion of Gentiles as fellow heirs in Christ.
Those who share equally in the inheritance promised by God, signifying unity and equality in salvation.
The infinite and incomprehensible blessings and grace found in Christ, beyond human understanding.
The many-sided and diverse wisdom of God displayed through the church to spiritual powers and the world.

outline.heading: Paul’s Role and the Mystery Revealed
outline.description: Paul identifies himself as a prisoner for the Gentiles and explains the revelation of the mystery that Gentiles are fellowheirs with Jews in Christ, a truth previously hidden but now disclosed by the Spirit.

outline.heading: Paul’s Ministry and the Purpose of the Mystery
outline.description: Paul describes his calling and grace to preach the unsearchable riches of Christ, emphasizing the church’s role in revealing God’s manifold wisdom to heavenly powers and encouraging believers not to be discouraged by his sufferings.

outline.heading: Paul’s Prayer for Spiritual Empowerment
outline.description: Paul prays for believers to be strengthened by the Spirit, to have Christ dwell in their hearts through faith, to grasp the vast dimensions of Christ’s love, and concludes with praise to God’s glory through the church.
